where: the pairing row — the 'Pairing code' label, the empty field, and the 'Approve this kiosk' button beside it (identical in kiosk-menu, kiosk-setup-denied and kiosk-setup-counselor)
finding: The field won size and lost presence. It is now the biggest box in the register, but at rest it is also the lowest-contrast object in it: an ink-900 fill on ink-950 is barely a surface, the six placeholder dots are ink-700 on that fill, and the label naming it is the smallest type in the whole form. The button next to it is a solid tinted slab with near-white-blue bold text. So the emphatic object in the pairing row is the control that cannot yet be pressed, and the live control it depends on is the quietest thing beside it. Squinting, the arrival order is h1, blue slab, field — third out of three on the screen whose entire job is that field. In the denied frame it is worse: a red panel above and a red badge below leave the form as a silent trough between two alarms.
evidence: Field box x=256–466, y=141–201 on ink-950; placeholder ink-700 on ink-900 is nearly invisible at 100%. Label is `pointer-fine:text-xs` ink-300 — smaller than the ink-400 hint below the button. Button is `disabled:bg-brand-500/20 disabled:text-brand-200` at x=483–668, and is the only filled, chromatic object above the rule in kiosk-setup and kiosk-menu.
direction: Do not undo the disabled primary's brand identity — that answered a real inversion. Give the field the presence instead, so the invitation sits on the thing that is actually live: a surface and edge that read as lit rather than as an inert well, a placeholder that shows six waiting slots rather than dissolving into the fill, and a label that is not the smallest type in its own group. The rank in this row should be field first, button second, at rest as well as after typing.

where: the page's two measures — the header/form register above the rule, and the rule plus the two-column core-team register below it (same in kiosk-menu and kiosk-setup-denied)
finding: At 1440 the page is composed at two widths and the wider one belongs to the reference material. Everything above the rule stops at x≈828; the rule itself runs to x=1407 and the subordinate register runs to x=1399, 32px off the window edge. The result is an empty upper-right quadrant roughly 580×280 next to the only content that matters, and a divider that is the longest single line in the frame — drawn under the narrowest block, extending 580px past anything it is separating. The top of the page still reads as a phone layout that grew; the bottom reads as desktop, which inverts what the register system was built to say.
evidence: Content right edges by band: header prose 828, form 668, hint 819, rule 1407, core-team register 1399, footer 736. Last content row y=614 of 900.
direction: Pick one measure for the page and let the registers differ by weight rather than by width. Either the subordinate register comes in to the measure the job occupies — so the rule ends where the content ends and the right margin is margin — or the job register earns the full width (the instruction, the field and the verdict line arranged across it) so the page has one right edge. A rule should not be wider than the wider of the two things it divides.

where: the two sections below the rule — 'This deployment' and 'Phone search' — and the small print under the second rule
finding: The subordinate register has no internal ramp and no consistency across its two columns. Two peer sections sit at the same y under identical 12px uppercase ink-500 headings, but one sets its body at 14px and the other at 12px, both at ink-500; the facts row under the first is 12px with ink-300 values, so within one block the largest text is the dimmest and the brightest is the smallest. Below the second rule the footer trivia is set at exactly the same 12px ink-500 as the phone-search paragraph, so background that nobody needs and the description of a live utility are typographically the same thing. Everything under the rule flattens to one grey.
evidence: 'Tally can hand a kiosk a session…' is `text-sm text-ink-500`; the Phone search paragraph is `text-xs leading-relaxed text-ink-500`; both footer paragraphs are `text-xs leading-relaxed text-ink-500`; the `dl` is `text-xs` with ink-500 terms and ink-300 values.
direction: Fix one body size for the whole subordinate register so peer sections read as peers, and let a single step of contrast — not size — distinguish a fact you may need to act on from the small print you will never read. If the footer is a lower rank than the register above it, it should look lower rather than identical.

where: the 'Check again' and 'Rebuild phone search index' buttons at the foot of the two core-team columns
finding: The two columns' terminal controls miss each other by 14px. They are the same object at the same rank in a two-column register, close enough that the eye expects a shared baseline and far enough that the offset reads as an accident rather than as staggering. It is the one thing in the lower half that makes the grid look assembled rather than set.
evidence: Check again occupies y=401–437; Rebuild phone search index y=415–451. Both `min-h-11 pointer-fine:min-h-9` in a `lg:grid lg:grid-cols-3 lg:items-start` row.
direction: Either let the two columns' actions share a baseline — pin them to the bottom of the row, or equalise what precedes them — or separate them enough that the difference is legible as a choice. A 14px offset is neither.

where: the header bar's wordmark and account chip against the page column beneath them
finding: The shared edge the rail-less layout was rebuilt for is 32px short of shared. The header's inner wrapper and the page column are both capped at the same measure, but the header pads by 16px and the page by 32px, so the wordmark starts 32px left of the h1 and the chip ends 32px right of the text column. Two structural elements a hair out of alignment read worse than two elements openly at different positions: the frame looks like it slipped rather than like it was set.
evidence: Wordmark left edge x=384, 'Pair a kiosk' left edge x=416; header is `px-4` with an inner `lg:max-w-2xl`, the page container is `lg:px-8` with `lg:max-w-2xl`.
direction: Make the header's inner measure resolve to the same content edges as the page column, not the same outer box — the two need to agree after padding, at both widths.

where: the 'Check in' link in the band between the two full-measure rules
finding: One 40px outline control is bracketed by two full-width rules 86px apart, with no heading and no companion. On the admin build that slot holds a labelled two-column register, so the rules earn themselves; here they fence off a mostly empty band around a single small button, which is exactly the shape of an unfinished section. It also arrives in the same quiet outline treatment the admin page gives 'Rebuild phone search index', so this role's only route onward is weighted like a maintenance utility.
evidence: Rules at y=361 and y=447; the link occupies y=381–421, x=416–536, inside a 608px measure. `border-t border-ink-800 pt-6` above, `border-t border-ink-800 pt-4` below.
direction: Either give the band something to be — a heading of the same species the admin register uses, so the rule has a section to introduce — or drop the rule and let the exit sit as the closing move of the page, with a weight that says destination rather than utility. Two rules should not enclose less content than the gap between them.

where: the danger banner above the field and the gcloud command block, against the page's left edge
finding: This page gave up cards so that every element could start on one left edge, and the two remaining padded boxes break it. The banner and the `pre` inset their text 12px, so the frame has text starting at x=256 for the h1, intro, label, headings, paragraphs and facts, and at x=268 for the two tinted panels — including the banner that sits directly between the intro and the field label, where the step is most visible. A single stray edge on the one screen whose composition is 'the content is the page' is the thing that makes it look assembled.
evidence: Banner box x=256–836 with `px-3`, text begins at x=268, sandwiched between intro text at 256 and 'Pairing code' at 256; the `pre` at x=256–1013 does the same.
direction: Let the tinted panels hang their padding outside the measure so their text keeps the page's left edge, or drop their fill and mark them by accent and position alone. The page has one column; nothing on it should start in a second place.

where: the stack inside 'This deployment' — badge, explanation, project/service-account facts, command block, buttons
finding: Five different kinds of content are set at one uniform 8px gap, so nothing in the block groups: the verdict, the explanation, the identifying facts, the remedy and the actions all sit at the same interval and read as one undifferentiated run. Worse, the facts row is wedged between the sentence that says 'grant it, then check again' and the command that grants it, so the reader's eye crosses a line of context in the middle of an instruction and its object — the same shape as the hint that used to sit between the field and its button.
evidence: `flex flex-col gap-2` on the section with h2, badge, `text-sm text-ink-300` paragraph, `dl`, `pre` and the button row as siblings; the dl at y≈494–507 sits directly between the explanation ending y≈482 and the pre beginning y≈516.
direction: Let the gaps do the grouping: verdict and explanation together, remedy and its actions together, and the deployment's identifying facts either before the whole diagnosis or after it — not in the gap between an instruction and the thing it points at.
